transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My mind just won’t shut off about work and everything else, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off no matter what I do. It has gotten to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed by all of my responsibilities, and I just don't know how to make it stop.
Do you ever experience sudden, intense episodes of fear or physical discomfort—such as a racing heart, chest tightness, or feeling like you might lose control—that peak within a few minutes?
No, I don't really experience those sudden, intense peaks of panic or physical symptoms like a racing heart. It’s more of a constant, lingering tension and feeling on edge throughout the whole day.
Beyond the constant worrying, have you noticed a persistent loss of interest or pleasure in the activities you usually enjoy, or do you feel a general sense of hopelessness or low mood?

I wouldn't say I've lost interest or feel hopeless, because I still really want to do the things I love like dancing and hiking. It's just that I feel so exhausted, drained, and anxious all the time that I don't have the energy to actually go out and do them right now.
Do you often find yourself experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, or difficulty falling or staying asleep because your mind is racing?

Yes, I feel constantly wired and on edge, to the point where I'm constantly clenching my shoulders and tapping my foot in meetings. At night, I lie awake until 2 a.m. staring at the ceiling and replaying work emails, and even when I do sleep, I wake up multiple times and feel completely unrefreshed.
For how many months have you been experiencing this persistent, excessive worry and physical tension on most days?
It's been going on for about nine months now. It pretty much started right when I got my promotion and took on all those extra responsibilities as the main bilingual contact for our major client.
